questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true for the Form Designer? a) To add a field to the form layout, drag the field from the Fields tab to the desired destination on the form. b) To create a new field on a form's table, drag the appropriate data type from the Field Types tab to the form and then configure the new field. c) To remove a field from the form layout, hover over the field to enable the Action buttons, and select the Delete (X) button. d) To add a section to the form layout, drag it from the Field Types tab to the desired destination on the form.

Which of the following are configured in an Email Notification? a) Who will receive the notification. b) What content will be in the notification. c) When to send the notification. d) How to send the notification.
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Email Notifications > Configuration: Email notifications configure who receives the notification, what content is in it, and when to send it (A). 'How to send' is not a configurable field — notifications always send via email. The notification form covers recipient conditions, message content/templates, and trigger/when criteria.

questions.stem: To see what scripts, reports, and other application artifacts will be in a published application:

options.text: Enter the name of the Application in the Global search field
Open the list of Update Sets for the instance
Examine the Application Files Related List in the application to be published
Open the artifact records individually to verify the value in the Application field

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Publishing > Artifacts: To see all scripts, reports, and artifacts before publishing, examine the Application Files Related List in the application record (C). This list shows every file in the application scope. Global search (A) and Update Sets (B) don't give a complete, scoped view of all application artifacts.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a debugging strategy for client-side scripts?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Debugging > Client-Side: gs.log() (D) is NOT a client-side debugging strategy — it is a server-side GlideSystem method used in Business Rules and Script Includes. Client-side debugging tools are: g_form.addInfoMessage() (A - form messages), Field Watcher (B - monitors field changes), and jslog() (C - outputs to browser console).

questions.stem: Which Application Access configuration field(s) are NOT available if the Can read configuration field is NOT selected?

options.text: All access to this table via web services
Can create, Can update, and Can delete
Can read does not affect the availability of other Application Access fields

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Access > Can Read Dependency: When 'Can read' is not selected, Can create, Can update, and Can delete (B) become unavailable. The doc at p74 confirms these options are 'available only when the Can read check box is selected.' Write access requires read access as a prerequisite. Allow configuration (D) is independent of Can read. (p74)

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a trigger type in Flow Designer?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Flow Designer > Trigger Types: Outbound Email (A) is NOT a Flow Designer trigger type — it is an action/step within a flow. Valid trigger types include: Record (C - record events), Schedule (D - time-based), and Application (B - application-level events). Flows are triggered by incoming events; outbound email is an output, not a trigger.

questions.stem: When creating new application files in a scoped application, cross scope access is turned on by default in which of the following?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Access > Cross-Scope Defaults: For new files in a scoped application, Tables (B) have cross-scope access enabled by default in their Application Access settings. Script Includes (C) default to 'This application scope only' in the Accessible from field. REST messages (A) and Workflows (D) do not enable cross-scope access by default.

questions.stem: In an Email Notification, which one of the following is NOT true for the Weight field?

options.text: Only Notifications with the highest weight for the same record and recipients are sent
A Weight value of zero means that no email should be sent
The Weight value defaults to zero
A Weight value of zero means the Notification is always sent when the Notification's When to send criteria is met

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Email Notifications > Weight Field: 'A Weight value of zero means no email should be sent' (B) is NOT true. A weight of zero means the notification is ALWAYS sent when its criteria is met (D - true). Only notifications with the highest weight for the same record and recipients are sent (A - true). Weight defaults to zero (C - true).

questions.stem: Which of the following objects does a Display Business Rule NOT have access to?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Business Rules > Display BR Objects: A Display Business Rule does NOT have access to the 'previous' object (A). The 'previous' object (prior field values) is only available in Before, After, and Async BRs. Display BRs have access to: current (the displayed record), g_scratchpad (client-server bridge), and GlideSystem (gs) methods.

questions.stem: Which of the following features are available to Global applications? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Global Applications > Features: Features available to Global applications are Automated Test Framework (A) and Flow Designer (D). Source Control (B) is only for scoped applications — global apps cannot be linked to source control repositories. Delegated Development (C) applies to scoped application management only.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a UI Action type?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > UI Actions > Types: 'Form choice' (D) is NOT a valid UI Action type. Valid types include: List banner button, List bottom button, List context menu, List choice (A), List link, Form button (B), Form link, Form context menu. The 'choice' type exists only for lists, not forms — there is no 'Form choice' type. (p2218)

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT supported by Flow Designer?

options.text: Call a subflow from a flow
Run a flow from a MetricBase Trigger

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Flow Designer > Limitations: Testing a flow with rollback (B) is NOT supported — Flow Designer testing executes the flow and does NOT roll back record changes. Flow Designer does support: calling subflows from a flow (A), Delegated Developer access (C), and running from a MetricBase Trigger (D).

questions.stem: Which of the following are true for reports in ServiceNow? (Choose three.)

options.text: Any user can see any report shared with them.
Can be a graphical representation of data.
All users can generate reports on any table.
Can be run on demand by authorized users.
Can be scheduled to be run and distributed by email.

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Reports > True Statements: Three true statements: reports can be graphical representations of data (B), run on demand by authorized users (D), and scheduled to run and distribute by email (E). 'Any user can see any report shared with them' (A) is false — users still need table/role access. 'All users can report on any table' (C) is false — roles are required.

questions.stem: Modules must have a Link type. Which one of the following is a list of Link types?

options.text: List of Records, Separator, Catalog Type, Roles
Assessment, List of Records, Separator, Timeline Page
List of Records, Content Page, Order, URL (from arguments:)
Assessment, List of Records, Content Page, Roles

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Modules > Link Types: The valid list of Module link types is Assessment, List of Records, Separator, and Timeline Page (B). The doc at p2386 confirms these as valid types. 'Catalog Type' and 'Roles' in option A are not link types; 'Order' in option C is not a link type; option D mixes valid and invalid entries. (p2386)

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true for a table with the `Allow configuration` Application Access option selected?

options.text: Only the in scope application's scripts can create Business Rules for the table
Any user with the application's user role can modify the application's scripts
Out of scope applications can create Business Rules for the table
Out of scope applications can add new tables to the scoped application

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Access > Allow Configuration: With 'Allow configuration' selected, out-of-scope applications can create Business Rules, Client Scripts, and other configuration records for that table (C). This grants cross-scope design-time access. It does not allow adding tables to the app (D) or provide general script or user write access (A, B). (p74)

questions.stem: When working in the Form Designer, configuring the label of a field in a child table changes the label on which table(s)?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Form Designer > Label Scope: When configuring a field label in a child table's Form Designer, the label change applies only to the child table (B). Each table in an inheritance hierarchy can maintain its own label overrides. Changing a child table's label does not modify the base table (A) or all tables (D) in the hierarchy.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true?

options.text: A UI Policy's Actions execute before the UI Policy's Scripts
The execution order for a UI Policy's Scripts and Actions is determined at runtime
A UI Policy's Scripts execute before the UI Policy's Actions
A UI Policy's Actions and Scripts execute at the same time

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > UI Policies > Execution Order: A UI Policy's Actions execute before the UI Policy's Scripts (A). Actions (field visibility, mandatory, read-only states) are applied first, then the script executes with those states in effect. This ordering allows scripts to react to or further modify the field states set by actions.

questions.stem:
Here is the Business Rule script template:

This type of JavaScript function is known as:
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Business Rules > Script Pattern: The Business Rule script template uses a self-invoking function (D) — an Immediately Invoked Function Expression (IIFE). The pattern (function executeRule(current, previous) { })(current, previous) automatically executes upon invocation. It is not a constructor (A), scoped function (B), or merely an anonymous function (C).

questions.stem: Which method call returns true only if the currently logged in user has the catalog_admin role and in no other case?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Client API > g_user.hasRoleExactly: g_user.hasRoleExactly('catalog_admin') (B) returns true ONLY if the user has that specific role directly assigned, bypassing admin role inheritance. g_user.hasRole() (A) returns true for admin users since admin inherits all roles. hasRoleOnly (C) and hasRoleFromList (D) are not valid g_user methods.

questions.stem: There is a basic strategy when creating a Utils Script Include. Identify the step that does not belong.

options.text: Create a prototype object from the new class

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Script Includes > Utils Pattern: 'Identify the table' (A) does not belong in the Utils Script Include creation process. The correct steps are: Create a class (C), Create a prototype object from the new class (D), and Script the function(s) (B). A Utils Script Include is a reusable utility class not tied to any specific table.

questions.stem:
Which roles grant access to source control repository operations such as importing applications from source control, or linking an application to source control?
(Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Source Control > Required Roles: Roles granting access to source control operations (import/link applications) are source_control (A) and admin (C). The doc at p982 lists these operations as available via Studio with appropriate permissions. source_control_admin (B) and git_admin (D) are not standard ServiceNow source control roles. (p982)

questions.stem: When configuring the content of an Email Notification, which syntax should be used to reference the properties of an event triggering the Notification?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Email Notifications > Event Property Syntax: In an email notification template, event properties are referenced using ${event.<property name>} syntax (A). For example, ${event.parm1} references the first event parameter. ${current.field} (B) accesses the triggering record's fields, and ${gs.method} (D) is not valid template syntax for event data.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true for a Script Include with a Protection Policy value of Protected?

options.text: Any user with the protected_edit role can see and edit the Script Include
The Protection policy option can only be enabled by a user with the admin role
The Protection Policy is applied only if the glide.app.apply_protection system property value is true
The Protection Policy is applied only if the application is downloaded from the ServiceNow App Store

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Script Include > Protection Policy: A Protection Policy of 'Protected' is applied only when the application is downloaded from the ServiceNow App Store (D). In the development environment, protection is not enforced. The protection hides/locks code when installed on customer instances from the Store. Only ServiceNow employees can alter the protection policy for ServiceNow-owned files. (p37)

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true for GlideUser (g_user) methods?

options.text: Can be used in Client Scripts and UI Policies only
Can be used in Business Rules only
Can be used in Client Scripts, UI Policies, and UI Actions
Can be used in Business Rules, and Scripts Includes

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > GlideUser (g_user) > Availability: g_user methods can be used in Client Scripts, UI Policies, and UI Actions (C). g_user is a client-side object available in all client-side execution contexts. It is not available in server-side scripts like Business Rules (B) or Script Includes (D) — those use gs (GlideSystem) instead.

questions.stem: When configuring a module, what does the Override application menu roles configuration option do?

options.text: Users with the module role but without access to the application menu access the module
Self-Service users can access the module even though they do not have roles
Admin is given access to the module even if Access Controls would ordinarily prevent access
Users with access to the application menu can see the module even if they don't have the module role

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Modules > Override Menu Roles: The 'Override application menu roles' option allows users who have the module's role but do NOT have permission to view the containing application menu to still access that module (A). The doc at p2384 confirms: 'Allows users to access this module even if they do not have permission to view the containing application menu.' Users still need the module's role. (p2384)

questions.stem: Which platform feature can be used to determine the relationships between field in an Import Set table to field in an existing ServiceNow table?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Import Sets > Transform Map: A Transform Map (C) determines the relationships between fields in an Import Set table and fields in an existing ServiceNow table. Transform Maps define how each source column maps to a destination field during data import/transformation. Business Service Management Maps (A) and CI Relationship Builder (D) are CMDB tools.

questions.stem: When configuring a REST Message, the Endpoint is:

options.text: The commands to the REST script to stop execution
The URI of the data to be accessed, queried, or modified
Information about the format of the returned data
The response from the provider indicating there is no data to send back

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > REST Messages > Endpoint: The Endpoint in a REST Message is the URI of the data to be accessed, queried, or modified (B). It specifies the URL where the REST call is directed. It is not a command to stop execution (A), format information (C), or an empty response indicator (D).

questions.stem: When evaluating Access Controls, ServiceNow searches and evaluates:

options.text: Only for matches on the current table
Only for matches on the current field
From the most specific match to the most generic match
From the most generic match to the most specific match

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Access Controls > Evaluation Order: When evaluating Access Controls, ServiceNow searches from the most specific match to the most generic match (C). It checks table.field first, then table.*, falling back to broader matches. The most specific ACL found determines access. It does NOT start with generic rules and work toward specific (D).

questions.stem: In a Business Rule, which one of the following returns true if the currently logged in user has the admin role?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Business Rules > Role Check: In a Business Rule, gs.hasRole('admin') (B) returns true if the currently logged-in user has the admin role. Business Rules are server-side, so the GlideSystem (gs) object is used. g_form methods (A, C) are client-side only. gs.hasRoleExactly() (D) would only return true if admin is explicitly assigned, not inherited.

questions.stem:
From the list below, identify one reason an application might NOT be a good fit with ServiceNow.
The application:

options.text: Requires ג€as-isג€ use of low-level programming libraries
Uses forms extensively to interact with data

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Fit > Poor Fit: Requiring 'as-is' use of low-level programming libraries (B) is a reason an application is NOT a good fit for ServiceNow. ServiceNow doesn't support arbitrary low-level library integration. Workflow management (A), reporting (C), and form-based data interaction (D) are all ServiceNow strengths and good reasons to build on the platform.

questions.stem: Identify the incorrect statement about Delegated Development in ServiceNow.

options.text: Administrators can grant non-admin users the ability to develop global applications.
Administrators can specify which application file types the developer can access.
Administrators can grant the developer access to script fields.
Administrators can grant the developer access to security records.

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Delegated Development > Incorrect Statement: 'Administrators can grant non-admin users the ability to develop global applications' (A) is incorrect. The doc at p191 confirms: 'Developer permissions are available only for scoped apps, not global apps.' Delegated development is exclusively for scoped applications. Admins CAN specify file types (B), grant script access (C), and grant security record access (D). (p191)

questions.stem: One of the uses of the ServiceNow REST API Explorer is:

options.text: Practice using REST to interact with public data providers
Find resources on the web for learning about REST
Convert SOAP Message functions to REST methods
Create sample code for sending REST requests to ServiceNow

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > REST API Explorer: One use of the ServiceNow REST API Explorer is to create sample code for sending REST requests to ServiceNow (D). The explorer generates example request code in multiple languages. It does not interact with public data providers (A), provide REST learning resources (B), or convert SOAP to REST (C).

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true regarding Application Scope?

options.text: All applications are automatically part of the Global scope
Applications downloaded from 3 party ServiceNow application developers cannot have naming conflicts rd
Any developer can edit any application
Developers can choose the prefix for a scope's namespace

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Scope: Applications downloaded from third-party ServiceNow developers cannot have naming conflicts (B) because scoped applications use unique namespace prefixes (x_company_appname format). This prefix isolation prevents collisions. Global applications CAN have naming conflicts. Not all apps are global scope (A is false). Any developer cannot edit any app (C is false). (p30)

questions.stem: Which one of the following is the baseline behavior of a table in a privately-scoped application?

options.text: The table and its data are not accessible using web services
Any Business Rule can read, write, delete, and update from the table
Only artifacts in the table's application can read from the table
All application scopes can read from the table

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Scoped Table Baseline: The baseline behavior of a privately-scoped table is that all application scopes can read from the table (D). By default, tables in scoped apps allow read access across scopes. Write operations (create, update, delete) require explicit Application Access grants. Tables are also accessible via web services by default (A is false). (p74)

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a purpose of application scoping?

options.text: Provide a relationship between application artifacts
Provide a way of tracking the user who developed an application
Provide a namespace (prefix and scope name) to prevent cross application name collisions
Provide controls for how scripts from another scope can alter tables in a scoped application

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Scope > Purposes: 'Provide a way of tracking the user who developed an application' (B) is NOT a purpose of application scoping. The purposes of scoping are: namespace/prefix to prevent naming conflicts (C), relationship between application artifacts (A), and controls for cross-scope script access (D). Developer tracking is done through other mechanisms. (p29)

questions.stem: It is best practice to define the business requirements and the process(es) an application will manage as part of the application development plan. What are some of the considerations to document as part of the business process?

options.text: Business problem, data input/output, users/stakeholders, and process steps
Business problem, data input/output, project schedule, and process steps
Business problem, data input/output, users/stakeholders, and database capacity
Business problem, users/stakeholders, available licenses, and database capacity

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Planning > Business Process Documentation: The business process documentation considerations are: business problem, data input/output, users/stakeholders, and process steps (A). Project schedule (B) is a project management artifact. Database capacity (C, D) is an infrastructure concern. These four elements define the core of a business process. (p615)

questions.stem: Which of the following statements does NOT apply when extending an existing table?

options.text: The parent table's Access Controls are evaluated when determining access to the new table's records and fields
The new table inherits the functionality built into the parent table
The new table inherits all of the fields from the parent table
You must script and configure all required behaviors

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Table Extension > What Applies: 'You must script and configure all required behaviors' (D) does NOT apply when extending a table. Inherited behaviors, fields, and ACLs come automatically from the parent. True statements are: parent ACLs are evaluated (A), functionality is inherited (B), and all parent fields are inherited (C). Table extension reduces the need to rebuild behaviors from scratch.

questions.stem: Which of the following CANNOT be debugged using the Field Watcher?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Field Watcher > Limitations: Script Includes (B) CANNOT be debugged directly with the Field Watcher. The Field Watcher traces scripts triggered by a field change — it shows Business Rules (A), Client Scripts (C), and Access Controls (D) that respond to field modifications. Script Includes are called by other scripts, not triggered independently by field changes.

questions.stem: Which objects can be used in Inbound Action scripts?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Inbound Actions > Available Objects: Inbound Action scripts have access to current (the record being created/updated) and email (the email object with sender, subject, body, attachments) (B). 'previous' is not available since inbound actions don't track prior record state. 'event' is for Script Actions. 'producer' is for Record Producer scripts.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is part of the client-side scripting API?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Client-Side API > g_user: The GlideUser object (g_user) (B) is part of the client-side scripting API. It provides user information and role-checking methods in Client Scripts and UI Policies. GlideSystem (gs) (D) is server-side. current and previous (C) are server-side Business Rule objects. workflow.scratchpad (A) is a workflow construct.

questions.stem: Application developers configure ServiceNow using industry standard JavaScript to`¦

options.text: Enable the right-click to edit the context menus on applications in the navigator
Customize the organization's company logo and banner text
Configure the outgoing email display name

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > JavaScript Usage: Application developers configure ServiceNow using JavaScript to extend and add functionality (B). JavaScript enables custom logic, automation, integrations, and process extensions beyond what baseline configuration provides. It does not control context menus (A), company branding (C), or email display names (D) which are system configuration settings.

questions.stem: How many applications menus can an application have?

options.text: 3, one for an application's user modules, one for an application's administrator modules, and one for the ServiceNow administrator's modules
As many as the application design requires
2, one for an application's user modules and one for an application's administrator modules
1, which is used for all application modules

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Menus: An application can have as many application menus as the design requires (B). There is no fixed limit of 1, 2, or 3 menus. Complex applications may need multiple menus for different user roles or functional areas. The count is determined entirely by application design requirements.

questions.stem: The source control operation used to store local changes on an instance for later application is called a(n) <blank>.
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Source Control > Stash: A stash (C) stores local changes on an instance for later application without committing them to the repository. A branch (A) maintains a separate version; a tag (B) permanently marks a version; update sets (D) are a different ServiceNow mechanism unrelated to Git source control operations.

questions.stem: What syntax is used in a Record Producer script to access values from Record Producer form fields?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Record Producer > Variable Access: In a Record Producer script, values from form variables are accessed using producer.field_name syntax (A). The producer object provides access to variables defined on the Record Producer form. current.field_name (D) accesses the destination record's fields, not the form input variables.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods prints a message on a blue background to the top of the current form by default?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > GlideForm API > addInfoMessage: g_form.addInfoMessage() (B) prints a message on a blue background banner at the top of the current form. g_form.addInfoMsg() (A) is not a valid method name. g_form.showFieldMessage() (C) shows a message next to a specific field, not the form banner. g_form.showFieldMsg() (D) is also not a valid method.

questions.stem: A scoped application containing Flow Designer content dedicated to a particular application is called a(n):
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Flow Designer > Spoke: A scoped application containing Flow Designer content (actions, subflows, flows) dedicated to a specific application or integration is called a Spoke (A). Spokes package related integration content together. A Bundle (B) groups catalog items; an Action (C) is a single flow step; a Flow (D) is the full automation process.

questions.stem: What is a Module?

options.text: The functionality within an application menu such as opening a page in the content frame or a separate tab or window
A group of menus, or pages, providing related information and functionality to end-users
A way of helping users quickly access information and services by filtering the items in the Application Navigator
A web-based way of providing software to end-users

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Navigation > Module Definition: A Module is the functionality within an application menu that opens a page in the content frame or a separate tab/window (A). Users click modules in the Application Navigator to access lists, forms, reports, or external URLs. A group of modules organized together forms an Application Menu.

questions.stem: Which source control operation is available from BOTH Studio and the Git Repository?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Source Control > Dual-Location Operations: Create Branch (A) is available from BOTH Studio and the Git Repository. The doc at p1378 explicitly shows Create Branch listed under both '? Studio ? GIT repository.' Apply Remote Changes (B) is App Engine Studio only. Stash Local Changes (C) is Studio only. (p1378)

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT required to link a ServiceNow application to a Git repository?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Source Control > Git Connection Requirements: The Application name (D) is NOT required to link an application to a Git repository — the application context is already set in Studio. Required fields are: URL (B - repository location), Username (C - Git authentication), and Password (A - Git authentication). (p560)

questions.stem: Which Report Type(s) can be created by right-clicking on a column header in a table's list?

options.text: Bar Chart, Pie Chart, Histogram, and Line
Bar Chart, Pie Chart, and Histogram

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Reports > Quick Creation: Right-clicking on a column header in a table's list allows creating Bar Chart and Pie Chart reports (D). These two types are the quick-create options available from the list column context menu. Histogram and Line charts (A, C) are not available via this right-click shortcut.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT a method used for logging messages in a server-side script for a privately-scoped application?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Logging > Scoped Apps: gs.log() (A) is NOT available in privately-scoped applications — it is restricted to global scope only. Scoped applications must use the scoped logging methods: gs.error() (B), gs.warn() (C), and gs.debug() (D). Using gs.log() in a scoped app will not function as expected.

questions.stem: If the Create module field is selected when creating a table, what is the new module's default behavior?

options.text: Open an empty form so new records can be created
Open a link to a wiki article with instructions on how to customize the behavior of the new module
Display an empty homepage for the application
Display a list of all records from the table

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Tables > Create Module Default: When 'Create module' is selected during table creation, the new module defaults to displaying a list of all records from the table (D). The module uses the 'List of Records' link type. It does not open an empty form for record creation (A) or display a homepage (C).

questions.stem: How must Application Access be configured to prevent all other private application scopes from creating configuration records on an application's data tables?

options.text: You must create Access Controls to prevent all other application scopes from creating configuration records on an application's data tables rather than using Application Access
Set the Accessible from field value to All application scopes and de-select the Can create option
Set the Accessible from field value to This application scope only and de-select the Allow access to this table via web services option
Set the Accessible from field value to This application scope only

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Access > Scope Restriction: To prevent all other private application scopes from creating configuration records on a table, set Accessible from to 'This application scope only' (D). The doc at p79 confirms this hides the table from other scopes during configuration record creation. ACLs (A) address runtime access, not design-time restrictions. (p79)

questions.stem: What are some of the benefits of extending an existing table such as the Task table when creating a new application? a) You can repurpose existing fields by simply changing the label. b) Use existing fields with no modifications. c) Existing logic from the parent table will be automatically applied to the new table. d) All of the parent table records are copied to the new table.
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Table Extension > Task Table Benefits: Benefits of extending the Task table are: repurpose existing fields by changing labels (a), use existing fields without modification (b), and inherit parent table logic/Business Rules (c) — making answer D (a, b, c). Parent records are NOT copied to child tables (d is false) — child tables maintain their own independent records.

questions.stem: When configuring an Access Control which has no condition or script, which one of the following statements is NOT true?

options.text: table.*will grant access to every field in a record
table.None will grant access to every record on the table
table.field will grant access to a specific field in a record
table.id will grant access to a specific record on the table

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Access Controls > Notation: 'table.id grants access to a specific record' (D) is NOT true — there is no .id ACL notation for specific records. True statements: table.* grants access to every field (A), table.None grants access to every record on the table (B), table.field grants access to a specific field (C). Specific record access requires conditions or scripts.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods are useful in Access Control scripts?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Access Controls > Script Methods: gs.hasRole() and current.isNewRecord() (B) are the useful Access Control script methods. Access Controls are server-side, so gs (not the client-side g_user) is correct. current.isNewRecord() checks if the record is being inserted. current.isNew() in options C and D is not a valid GlideRecord method — isNewRecord() is correct.

questions.stem: Which one of the following client-side scripts apply to Record Producers?

options.text: Catalog Client Scripts and Catalog UI Policies
UI Scripts and Record Producer Scripts

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Record Producers > Client Scripts: Catalog Client Scripts and Catalog UI Policies (A) apply to Record Producers since they are catalog items. Regular Client Scripts and UI Policies (D) only run on standard database table forms. UI Scripts (B, C) are global JavaScript includes, not form-level execution scripts.

questions.stem: When a ServiceNow instance requests information from a web service, ServiceNow is the web service:
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Web Services > Consumer: When ServiceNow requests information from an external web service, ServiceNow is the Consumer (D) — it calls and receives data from the external service. The external system providing the data is the Provider/Publisher. Consumer = requests the service; Provider = hosts and serves the data.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is the fastest way to create and configure a Record Producer?

options.text: Create a Catalog Category, open the category, and select the Add New Record Producer button
Use the Record Producer module then add and configure all variables manually
Open the table in the Table records and select the Add to Service Catalog Related Link
Open the table's form, right-click on the form header, and select the Create Record Producer menu item

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Record Producers > Fastest Creation: The fastest way to create a Record Producer is to open the table and select the 'Add to Service Catalog' Related Link (C). This automatically creates a Record Producer with the table's fields pre-mapped as variables. Manual creation via the Record Producer module (B) requires adding all variables individually.

questions.stem: Which objects can you use in a Scheduled Script Execution (Scheduled Job) script?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Scheduled Jobs > Available Objects: In a Scheduled Script Execution, available objects are GlideSystem (gs) and GlideRecord (C). Scheduled jobs run without a record context, so 'current' (in options A and D) is not available. GlideRecord queries tables for data, and GlideSystem handles logging, messages, and utility functions.

questions.stem: Can inherited fields be deleted from a table?

options.text: Yes, select the red X in the left-most column in the table definition
Yes, but only if they are text fields
Yes, but only if there has never been any saved field data
No, inherited fields cannot be deleted from a child table

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Tables > Inherited Fields: Inherited fields CANNOT be deleted from a child table (D). They are defined in parent tables and are part of the schema hierarchy. Only fields specifically created on the child table can be deleted there. This is a fundamental ServiceNow table inheritance principle.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the Application Picker?

options.text: Select an application as a favorite in the Application Navigator
Choose an application to edit and set the Application Scope
Choose an application to download and install

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Picker > Purpose: The Application Picker allows you to choose an application to edit and set the Application Scope (C). All subsequent configuration changes are attributed to the selected application. It is not for running apps (A), marking favorites (B), or downloading/installing (D) — those are separate functions in the Application Manager.

questions.stem: What are Application Files in a ServiceNow application?

options.text: An XML export of an application's table records
CSV files containing data imported into an application
XML exports of an application's Update Set

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Files > Definition: Application Files are ServiceNow artifacts comprising an application (C). They include configuration records like business rules, client scripts, UI policies, and roles that define the application's logic and behavior. XML table record exports (A, D) and CSV import files (B) are different concepts unrelated to Application Files.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT true for Modules?

options.text: Access to Modules is controlled with roles
Every Module must be part of an Application Menu
Every Module must be associated with a table

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Modules > Requirements: 'Every Module must be associated with a table' (D) is NOT true. Modules support many link types including URL, Script, HTML, Content Page, and more — not all require a table association. Modules do open content pages (A), access is controlled by roles (B, per p2384), and every module must belong to an Application Menu (C).

questions.stem: A graphical view of relationships among tables is a <blank>.
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Schema Map > Definition: A Schema map (A) is a graphical view of relationships among tables. It shows how tables relate to each other through reference fields and table extensions. Dependency view (B) and Map source report (D) are not standard ServiceNow tools. Graphical User Interface (C) is too generic and unrelated.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true for the Application Picker?

options.text: All custom application scope and the Global scope appear in the Application Picker
All applications in ServiceNow, including baseline applications like Incident, appear in the Application Picker
Only custom applications appear in the Application Picker
Only downloaded applications appear in the Application Picker

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Picker > Contents: All custom application scopes AND the Global scope appear in the Application Picker (A). This allows developers to switch between custom app contexts and the global scope. Baseline system apps like Incident do not appear as separate scope options (B is false). The picker is not limited to only custom (C) or only downloaded (D) applications.

questions.stem: When creating an application through the Guided Application Creator, which of the following is a user experience option?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Guided Application Creator > UX Options: Mobile (B) is a user experience option when creating an application through the Guided Application Creator. The GAC presents UX type options including Mobile for building applet-based mobile experiences. Portal (A) and Workspace (D) are also UX types, but the question's context points to Mobile as the specific answer. Self-service (C) is a use case, not a UX format.

questions.stem: When writing a Client Script to provide feedback targeted at a specific field, which method should be used?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > GlideForm > Field Feedback: g_form.showFieldMsg() (B) should be used to provide feedback targeted at a specific field. It displays a message directly adjacent to the named field on the form. g_form.showInfoMessage() (A) and g_form.addInfoMessage() (C) display banner messages at the top of the form, not field-specific. g_form.addFieldMsg() (D) is not a valid GlideForm method.

questions.stem: Which actions can a Business Rule take without scripting?

options.text: Set field values and write to the system log
Set field values and generate an event
Set field values and add message
Set field values and query the database

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Business Rules > No-Script Actions: A Business Rule can set field values AND add messages (C) without scripting. These are available in the BR Actions tab as declarative options. Writing to the system log (A) requires gs.log(). Generating an event (B) requires gs.eventQueue(). Querying the database (D) requires GlideRecord scripting. Only set field values and add message are no-script BR actions.

questions.stem: Which server-side object provides methods for working with dates when writing a script in a privately scoped application?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Scoped APIs > Dates: GlideDateTime (A) provides methods for working with dates and times in server-side scripts within privately scoped applications. It is a scoped server-side API. GlideRecord (B) is for database operations. GlideSystem/gs (C) provides utility methods but not comprehensive date handling. current (D) is the record object, not a date API.

questions.stem: Application developers can specify which ServiceNow page a user sees after submitting a new record using the Record Producer UI. How is the page specified?

options.text: Create an application property to store the URL
Configure the page in the Module that opens the Record Producer UI
Write an after Business Rule script for the Record Producer's table: window.redirect = "<URL>";
Write a script in the Record Producer's Script field: producer.redirect = "<URL>";

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Record Producer > Redirect: To specify the page a user sees after submitting a Record Producer, write a script in the Record Producer's Script field using producer.redirect = '<URL>' (D). The producer object is available in Record Producer scripts for controlling post-submission behavior. Application properties (A) and module configuration (B) don't control this. window.redirect (C) is not a server-side construct.

questions.stem: Identify characteristic(s) of a Record Producer. (Choose three.)

options.text: All records created using this strategy are inserted into the Requested Item [sc_req_item] table.
Each field prompts the user with a question rather than a field label.
You can script behaviors of fields in the user interface.
Graphics can be included on the user interface.

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Record Producers > Characteristics: Three characteristics are: each field prompts users with a question rather than a field label (B), you can script field behaviors using Catalog Client Scripts/UI Policies (D), and graphics/images can be included on the interface (E). Records are NOT always inserted into sc_req_item (A is false — any table can be the target). Scripting is optional (C is false).

questions.stem: Which server-side API debug log method is available for scoped applications?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > GlideSystem > Scoped Logging: gs.info() (B) is the server-side API debug log method available in scoped applications. gs.log() (A) is restricted in scoped apps — it is a global-only method. gs.debuglog() (C) and gs.print() (D) are not valid GlideSystem methods. In scoped apps, use gs.info(), gs.warn(), or gs.error() for logging.

questions.stem: Which script types execute on the server? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Script Execution > Server vs Client: Three script types that execute on the server are Business Rules (A), Script Actions (D), and Scheduled Jobs (E). Client Scripts (B) execute in the user's browser (client-side). UI Policies (C) also execute client-side in the browser. Business Rules, Script Actions, and Scheduled Jobs all run server-side against the database.

questions.stem: What is the best UX format to use for lists and forms?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > UX Formats > Lists and Forms: Classic (D) is the best UX format for lists and forms in ServiceNow. The Classic UI provides the traditional form and list experience built on the standard ServiceNow framework. Forms (A) and Lists (B) are content types, not UX formats. Standard (C) is not a recognized UX format designation for the form/list experience.

questions.stem: When creating a table in a privately-scoped application, which four Access Controls are created for the table?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Table Creation > Default ACLs: When creating a table in a privately-scoped app, four ACLs are created: Create, Delete, Read, Write (B). These correspond to the four standard ServiceNow table-level ACL operations. The docs (p742-743) confirm Create, Read, Write, Delete as the access control operations for table data. 'Insert/Query/Update' (A, C, D) use non-standard operation names.

questions.stem:
Which one of the following is true for this script fragment?
g_user.hasRole('x_my_app_user');

options.text: The method returns false only if the currently logged in user has the x_my_app_user role
The method returns true only if the currently logged in user has the x_my_app_user role
The method returns true if the currently logged in user has the x_my_app_user role or the admin role

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > g_user > hasRole Behavior: g_user.hasRole('x_my_app_user') returns true if the logged-in user has x_my_app_user OR the admin role (D). The hasRole() method grants automatic pass-through for admin users, similar to gs.hasRole() on the server side. To check ONLY the specific role without admin inheritance, use g_user.hasRoleExactly(). The method does exist (A is false).

questions.stem: Which one of the following database operations cannot be controlled with Application Access?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Access > Operations: Query (A) is the database operation that CANNOT be controlled with Application Access. Application Access provides checkboxes for Can read, Can create, Can update, and Can delete — but not Query. Query/read access control is managed via Access Control Lists (ACLs) and before-query Business Rules, not Application Access settings.

questions.stem: For Application Access there is a configuration option called Allow access to this table via web services. Which one of the following statements is true when this option is selected?

options.text: This option restricts the ability to delete records via web services but records can always be read
Even when not selected, users with the correct permissions can use web services to access the table's records
This option restricts access only to SOAP web services but does not apply to REST
The user performing the query via web services must have the correct permissions to access the table's records

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Access > Web Services: When 'Allow access to this table via web services' is selected, users performing web service queries must still have the correct permissions to access the table's records (D). Enabling web service access does not bypass ACLs or role requirements. It does not restrict only deletes (A), does not apply only to SOAP (C). Without selection, web service access is blocked regardless of permissions.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements must evaluate to true for a user to pass an Access Control? (Choose three.)

options.text: The user has one of the roles specified in the Required roles related list.
Scripts configured in the Access Control must evaluate to true.
Other matching Access Controls for the records evaluate to true.
Conditions configured in the Access Control must evaluate to true.
The user must be granted access through a business rule.

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Access Controls > Pass Requirements: For a user to pass an ACL, all three of the following must evaluate to true: the user has a required role (A), scripts evaluate to true (B), and conditions evaluate to true (D). All three elements must pass — if any fails, access is denied. Other matching ACLs (C) are evaluated independently. Business rule grants (E) are not part of ACL evaluation.

questions.stem: What is a workflow context?

options.text: The table for which a workflow is defined plus any conditions such as "Active is true"
It is generated from a workflow version, executes activities, and follows transitions
The business reason or process for which a workflow is designed
It is a checked out workflow which is being edited

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Workflows > Context Definition: A workflow context is generated from a workflow version, executes activities, and follows transitions (B). It is the runtime instance of a workflow executing for a specific record. The table/conditions define the workflow trigger (A). The business reason is the use case (C). A checked-out workflow is a draft/version under edit (D).

questions.stem: Which one of the following is a benefit of creating an Application Properties page for each application you develop?

options.text: Application Properties allow a developer to override the application properties inherited from ServiceNow
An Application Properties page is a good landing page for an application
Application Properties allow a developer or admin to make changes to an application's behavior without modifying application artifacts
Application users know to go to the Application Properties page to change the appearance of an application

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Properties: Application Properties allow a developer or admin to change application behavior without modifying application artifacts (C). Properties store configurable values (like settings) that scripts reference, so behavior can be tuned by updating a property value rather than editing each script. They are not a landing page (B) and do not override ServiceNow defaults (A).

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT an example of when an application might use a Scheduled Script Execution (Scheduled Job)?

options.text: The application needs to send weekly email reminders to requestors for all records on a table
The application needs to run a clean up script on the last day of every month
The application needs to query the database every day to look for unassigned records
The application needs to run a client-side script at the same time every day

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Scheduled Jobs: Running a client-side script at the same time every day (D) is NOT a valid Scheduled Job use case. Scheduled Jobs are server-side scripts; client-side scripts run in the browser and cannot be scheduled on the server. Sending weekly emails (A), running monthly cleanup (B), and querying for unassigned records (C) are all valid server-side scheduled job use cases.

questions.stem: Which one of the following objects CANNOT be used in a Script Action script?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Script Actions: The 'previous' object (A) CANNOT be used in a Script Action script. 'previous' is only available in Before/After/Async Business Rules to track prior field values. Script Actions are event-triggered and have access to: current (the triggering record), event (the event object), and GlideRecord for queries.

questions.stem: How does ServiceNow match inbound email to existing records?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Inbound Email > Watermark: ServiceNow matches inbound email replies to existing records using a watermark (A) — a unique identifier embedded in the outbound email thread. When a reply is received, the platform reads the watermark to identify which record the email belongs to and updates it accordingly.

questions.stem: When debugging Email Notifications, what must you check on a user record? (Choose three.)

options.text: The First name and Last name fields must have values.
The value in the Notification field must be set to enabled.
The user must not be locked out.
The Email field must have a value.

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Email Notification Debugging > User Record: When debugging email notifications, check: Active must be true (A - inactive users receive no notifications), Notification field must be Enabled (C - users can disable notifications), and Email field must have a value (E - required for delivery). First/Last name (B) and locked-out status (D) do not affect email delivery.

questions.stem: What are web services?

options.text: Methods used to create and maintain UI Pages
Methods used to allow applications to connect to other software applications over a network
Methods used to discover a wide variety of systems and applications
They provide a customer-facing view of available service and product offerings provided by departments within the organization

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Web Services > Definition: Web services are methods used to allow applications to connect to and communicate with other software applications over a network (B). They enable system-to-system integration using standardized protocols such as REST and SOAP. They are not UI page utilities (A) or discovery tools (C).

questions.stem: Which of the following methods is NOT part of the ServiceNow REST API?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > REST API > HTTP Methods: COPY (A) is NOT part of the ServiceNow REST API. COPY is a WebDAV extension method, not a standard REST HTTP method. Standard REST methods supported by ServiceNow include: GET (C is not C here - GET is B), POST (D), PUT, PATCH, and DELETE (C). COPY is not in the standard REST method set.

questions.stem:
You are developing the MyApp application that has a table, Table A. When the MyApp application is installed on an instance, you want Table A's records to be installed as part of the application.
Table A's records will be installed when:

options.text: Table A is active and extends the Task table
Table A's records are added to the application record using the Create Application Files context menu item
Table A has an automatic number counter for new records
Table A is not included in the System Clone > Exclude Tables list

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Data > Including Records: Table A's records will be installed as part of the application when they are added to the application record using the Create Application Files context menu item (B). Application data records must be explicitly included in the app. Simply having an active table (A) or auto-number counter (C) does not include the records. (p34)

questions.stem: How can an application link to a repository behind a firewall?

options.text: Link an application to source control through a MID Server.
Link an application to source control through an access token.
Link an application to source control with multi-factor authentication.

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Source Control > Firewall Access: An application can link to a repository behind a firewall by using a MID Server (B). The doc at p752 confirms: 'Use an existing MID Server to connect to a source control repository. Accessing an application through a MID Server enables access to repositories behind a firewall.' Access tokens (C) and MFA (D) do not solve firewall connectivity. (p752)

questions.stem: What is the ServiceNow store?

options.text: Alternate name for the ServiceNow Developer Share site
The source for ServiceNow Community created developer content
Marketplace for free and paid certified ServiceNow applications and integrations

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > ServiceNow Store: The ServiceNow Store is the marketplace for free and paid certified ServiceNow applications and integrations (D). Developers and partners publish certified apps that customers can download and install. It is not a script archive (A), the Developer Share site (B), or community content (C).

questions.stem: Tables that extend a table do what?

options.text: Do not inherit the parent’s fields

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Table Inheritance: Tables that extend another table inherit the parent's fields (D). All fields defined on a parent table are automatically available on child tables. This is fundamental to ServiceNow's table inheritance model. Child tables never skip field inheritance (C), and extending a table does not affect application scope (A).

questions.stem: When creating an application through the Guided Application Creator, which of the following is NOT an option for creating a table?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Guided Application Creator > Table Options: 'Create table from template' (A) is NOT an option in the Guided Application Creator. The available options are: Create table from scratch (B), Extend an existing table (C), and Upload spreadsheet (D). The doc at p668 confirms these three approaches for creating application data tables. (p668)

questions.stem: Server-side scripts manage what?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Server-Side Scripts > Scope: Server-side scripts manage the database and backend (A). They execute on the ServiceNow server and interact directly with database records, business logic, and data processing. Client-side scripts manage forms and fields (D). Access controls manage user access (C). Server-side scripts are not involved in Playbook access (B).

questions.stem: What intuitive development interface guides users through the initial application development process?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Development Tools > Guided Application Creator: The Guided Application Creator (B) is the intuitive development interface that guides users through the initial application development process step by step. ServiceNow Studio (C) is for more experienced developers without guided steps. Flow Designer (D) is for automation, and Guided Tour Designer (A) creates in-app help tours.

questions.stem: What are some benefits of developing private, scoped applications? (Choose two.)

options.text: To avoid using a code repository like GitHub or GitLab
To reduce risk at code collisions
To enable installation and uninstallation of an application
To replicate ServiceNow functions a private scope

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Scoped Applications > Benefits: Two benefits of private scoped applications are: reducing the risk of code collisions through namespace isolation (B), and enabling clean installation and uninstallation as a packaged unit (C). Scoped apps fully support source control (A is wrong). Replicating ServiceNow functions (D) is not a scoping benefit.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is NOT true for the Form Designer?

options.text: To add a section to the form layout, drag it from the Field Types tab to the desired destination on the form.
To add a field to the form layout, drag the field from the Fields tab to the desired destination on the form.
To remove a field from the form layout, hover over the field to enable the Action buttons, and select the Delete (X) button.
To create a new field on a form’s table, drag the appropriate data type from the Field Types tab to the form and then configure the new field.

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Form Designer > Sections: 'To add a section, drag it from the Field Types tab' (A) is NOT true. In Form Designer, sections are added via the form's section controls/buttons, not dragged from the Field Types tab. The Field Types tab is for creating NEW fields by dragging data types. Adding fields (B), removing fields (C), and creating new fields from types (D) are all true. (p1539)

questions.stem: What records are used to track cross-scope applications or scripts that request access to an application, application resource, or event?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Cross-Scope Access > Tracking Records: Restricted caller access records [sys_restricted_caller_access] (A) track cross-scope applications or scripts that request access to an application, resource, or event. The doc at p83 explicitly states this. They are created when Caller Restriction or Caller Tracking is set and a cross-scope script attempts access. (p83)

questions.stem: Which ATF Test step allows you to create a user with speeded roles and groups for the test?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > ATF > Create User Step: The 'Create a user' ATF test step (C) allows creating a test user with specified roles and groups for the test execution. This ensures tests run with precisely controlled user permissions without relying on existing user accounts. Impersonation (B) switches to an existing user rather than creating one.

questions.stem: What plugin enables the Guided Application Creator?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Guided Application Creator > Plugin: The plugin that enables the Guided Application Creator is com.glide.sn-guided-app-creator (A). This plugin activates the guided interface for walking developers through the initial application creation process. The other plugin identifiers (B, C, D) are not the correct plugin ID for this feature.

questions.stem: Which of the following can be an external data source for a ServiceNow application?

options.text: Data provided by a public web service using SOAP or REST

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > External Data Sources: ServiceNow supports all of the above as external data sources: Microsoft Excel files (A), data from public web services via SOAP or REST (B), and CSV files (C) — making the answer D (all of the above). The doc at p699 confirms Excel, CSV, and REST/SOAP as valid import source types. (p699)

questions.stem: Which one of the following is true for the Application Picker and Application Scope?

options.text: Global is a reserved application which does not appear in the Application Picker
Selecting an application from the Application Picker does not set the Application Scope
Selecting an application from the Application Picker sets the Application Scope
Selecting Global in the Application Picker sets the Application Scope to Incident

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Picker > Scope: Selecting an application from the Application Picker sets the Application Scope (C). All configuration changes are then attributed to that application. Global does appear in the picker (A is false). Selecting from the picker DOES set the scope (B is false). Selecting Global sets scope to Global, not Incident (D is false).

questions.stem: Which of the following is an available feature in Studio? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Studio > Available Features: Two available Studio features are Search code (C) — Studio has built-in code search to find snippets across app files — and Push to external source control (D) — Studio integrates with Git to push/pull changes. Push to update set (A) is an update set mechanism, not a Studio-specific feature. Branch merging (B) is explicitly NOT supported per the docs (p1428).

questions.stem: The Task table is an example of which of the following? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Task Table > Classification: The Task table is both a parent class (A) and a base class (D). Task is the foundational table from which other task-type tables (Incident, Problem, Change) extend, making it both the parent/ancestor in the hierarchy and the base class for task records. Legacy class (B) and child class (C) do not describe the Task table's role.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about deleting fields from a table?

options.text: Table records are deleted when a field is deleted
User-defined non-inherited fields can be deleted
Any field on a table can be deleted

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Table Fields > Deletion: User-defined non-inherited fields can be deleted (B). Fields that were explicitly added to a table (not inherited from a parent) can be removed. Deleting a field does NOT delete table records (A is false). Not any field can be deleted (C is false). Inherited fields specifically cannot be deleted (D is false) — they are owned by the parent table.

questions.stem: Why would you build a custom app? (Choose two.)

options.text: To avoid using a code repository like GitHub or GitLab
To fulfill a specific use case on internal processes
To create a custom integration for a 3rd party system

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Custom App > Reasons: Two valid reasons to build a custom app are: to fulfill a specific use case on internal processes (C) — ServiceNow enables apps tailored to unique business needs — and to create a custom integration for a 3rd party system (D). Avoiding code repositories (A) is not a reason — ServiceNow encourages source control. Replacing base tables (B) is not a valid design approach.

questions.stem: What are three ServiceNow table creation methods? (Choose three.)

options.text: Upload and turn a spreadsheet into a custom table
Use the Now Experience Table Creator

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Table Creation > Methods: Three table creation methods are: upload and turn a spreadsheet into a custom table (B), extend a table (E), and create a custom table from scratch (F). Legacy Workflows (A) and Flow Designer (C) are automation tools, not table creation methods. 'Now Experience Table Creator' (D) is not a recognized table creation mechanism.

questions.stem: When selecting a data type for a field that will be displayed on a form, which of the following statements is NOT correct?

options.text: Use the String data type tor a free-form text field
Use the Phone Number data type to automate phone number data validation
Use the Choice data type to limit options in a field
Use the Date data type to enter the date and time of day

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Field Data Types > Date vs Date/Time: 'Use the Date data type to enter the date and time of day' (D) is NOT correct. The Date field stores date only (no time component). To store both date and time, use the Date/Time field type. String (A) for free-form text, Phone Number (B) for phone validation, and Choice (C) for limiting options are all correct statements.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is NOT part of the Form Designer?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Form Designer > Components: The Schema map (B) is NOT part of the Form Designer. The Schema map is a separate tool in Studio that shows table relationships. Form Designer consists of: a page header (A), field navigator/types panel (C), and the form layout canvas (D). The Schema map is accessed independently and is not a Form Designer component.

questions.stem: Which class is NOT part of the Client side scoped APIs?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Client-Side APIs > GlideRecord: GlideRecord (C) is NOT part of the client-side scoped APIs — it is primarily a server-side API for database operations. The client-side scoped APIs include: GlideDialogWindow (A) for dialog boxes, GlideAjax (B) for client-to-server communication, and GlideForm/g_form (D) for form manipulation. GlideRecord runs against the database server-side.

questions.stem: When designing and creating a form what do you create to organize fields on a form?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Form Design > Sections: Sections (C) are created to organize fields on a form. Forms are divided into sections which group related fields together and can be collapsed. Buttons (A) trigger actions, Tabs (B) are used in workspaces/related lists, and Related lists (D) display records from associated tables — none of these organize fields in the form body.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is a good practice for adding instructions to a form?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Form Design > Instructions: Annotations (C) are the best practice for adding instructions to a form. Annotations allow instructional text to be embedded directly within the form layout. The docs (p1536) list annotations as a Form Designer option for adding text. Related links (A) navigate away; Context Menu UI Actions (B) are for record operations; read-only fields (D) waste a field slot.

questions.stem: Which of the following GlideRecord methods run a query against a database table? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > GlideRecord > Query Methods: Three GlideRecord methods that run a query are: query() (C) — standard method to execute a query and return multiple results; _query() (D) — an internal/underlying query method; and get() (E) — retrieves a single record by sys_id or field/value pair. _get() (A) and runQuery() (B) are not valid GlideRecord method names.

questions.stem: What is the GlideForm Client-side scripting object?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > GlideForm > Object Reference: The GlideForm client-side scripting object is referenced as g_form (B). Client Scripts and UI Policies use g_form to manipulate form fields (getValue, setValue, setVisible, setMandatory, etc.). sn.form (A) and gs_form (D) do not exist. gs (C) is GlideSystem, a server-side object.

questions.stem: In a Business Rule, which one of the following returns the sys_id of the currently logged in user?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > GlideSystem > getUserID: In a Business Rule, gs.getUserID() (C) returns the sys_id of the currently logged-in user. Business Rules are server-side and use the gs (GlideSystem) object. g_form.getUserID() (A) and g_form.getUserSysID() (D) are client-side methods not available in Business Rules. gs.getUserSysID() (B) is not the correct method name.

questions.stem: Access Control debug information identifies whether each element of an Access Control granted or denied access. The elements appear in the debug information in the order of evaluation. In which order are the elements of an Access Control evaluated?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Access Controls > Evaluation Order: The elements of an Access Control are evaluated in the order: Roles, Conditions, Script (C). All three must pass for access to be granted. Roles are checked first, then Conditions, and finally Script. This order is visible in ACL debug output. If Roles fails, evaluation stops — Conditions and Script are not checked.

questions.stem:
Assume a table called table exists and contains 3 fields: field1, field2, field3. Examine the Access Control list for table:



Which field or fields can a user with the itil role read?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Access Controls > Field-Level ACL: Based on the ACL table shown, a user with the itil role can read field3 only (D). The table.* or field1/field2 ACLs require roles that itil doesn't have, but a specific table.field3 ACL grants access to the itil role. ServiceNow evaluates the most specific ACL match — field-level ACLs override table-level ACLs for that specific field.

questions.stem:
Assume a table called table exists and contains 3 fields: field1, field2, field3. Examine the Access Control list for table:



Which field or fields can a user with the itil role read?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Access Controls > Field-Level ACL: Based on the ACL table shown, a user with the itil role can read all fields except field3 (D). The table.* ACL allows itil access to all fields by default, but table.field3 has a more restrictive ACL that requires a role itil does not have. The field-specific ACL for field3 overrides the permissive table.* rule for that field.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a caller access field option?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Script Include > Caller Access Options: 'Caller Permission' (D) is NOT a valid caller access field option. The three valid options are: None (C) — access per Accessible from field; Caller Restriction (B) — calls must be manually approved; and Caller Tracking (A) — calls are tracked. The doc at p85 lists exactly these three options. 'Caller Permission' does not exist.

questions.stem: Which method is used to retrieve Application Property values in a script?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Properties > Retrieval: gs.getProperty() (A) is used to retrieve Application Property values in a server-side script. This GlideSystem method returns the value of a named system/application property. g_form methods (B, C) are client-side and not used for property retrieval. gs.getAppProperty() (D) is not a valid GlideSystem method name.

questions.stem: What Module Link type is used to access an Application Properties page?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Modules > Application Properties Link: The URL (from Arguments) link type (C) is used to access an Application Properties page via a module. The Arguments field contains the sys_properties_category URL path. Single Record (A) opens a specific table record. HTML (from Arguments) (B) is for inline HTML. Script (from Arguments) (D) executes JavaScript — not a static URL.

questions.stem:
Identify the way(s) an application can respond to an Event generated by the gs.eventQueue() method.

a. Script Action
b. Scheduled Script Execution (Scheduled Job)
c. UI Policy
d. Email Notification
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Events > Responses: An application can respond to an event generated by gs.eventQueue() via Script Action (a) and Email Notification (d) — answer C. Script Actions execute server-side scripts when an event fires. Email Notifications can be triggered by events. Scheduled Jobs run on a schedule, not events. UI Policies are client-side form logic, not event responders.

questions.stem: When troubleshooting and debugging notifications, where do you navigate to see if an email was sent m response to an event?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Email Debugging > Email Log: To see if an email was sent in response to an event, navigate to System Logs > Emails (B). This log shows all outbound and inbound email activity. System Logs > Events (A) shows event records but not the resulting emails. Push Notifications (C) and ICE Logs (D) are unrelated to standard email.

questions.stem:
What are the benefits of storing the majority of an Application’s server-side script logic in a Script Include?

a. This makes execution faster.
b. Only run when called from a script.
c. The script logic can be hidden when the Application is installed from the ServiceNow Store. d. For some changes to application logic there is only one place to make edits.
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Script Includes > Benefits: The three benefits of storing logic in Script Includes are: b (only runs when called — loaded on demand), c (logic can be hidden when installed from the Store), and d (single place to edit logic for maintenance). Making execution faster (a) is NOT a benefit — Script Includes don't inherently speed up execution.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a Flow Designer feature?

options.text: Run a flow from a Catalog item
Call a flow from another flow or subflow
Test a flow using the “Run as” feature

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Flow Designer > Not Supported: Calling a flow from another flow or subflow (B) is NOT supported in Flow Designer. You can call SUBFLOWS from flows, but flows themselves are top-level and cannot be invoked from other flows. Flow Designer does support: running from a Catalog item (A), adding stages to a flow (C), and testing with Run as (D).

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the coalesce field when importing data?

options.text: If a match is not found, the existing record is updated
To determine if a record matches an existing record or is a new record
To identify and merge duplicate records
When a match is found, a new record is inserted

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Data Import > Coalesce: The coalesce field in a transform map determines if an incoming record matches an existing record or is a new record (B). If a match is found, the existing record is updated; if no match, a new record is inserted. Coalesce does NOT merge duplicates (C) — it prevents creating duplicate records during import.

questions.stem: If you create a SOAP Message what syntax indicates a variable to pass when the function is called?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > SOAP Messages > Variable Syntax: In SOAP Messages, variables are indicated using the ${variable_name} syntax (B). When the function is called, the variable placeholder is replaced with the actual value passed. The current.variable_name syntax (A) is for Business Rules, not SOAP message templates.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a way to install an application on a ServiceNow instance?

options.text: Install an application from the Application Repository
Select the Copy button on the application record
Download and install an application from the ServiceNow Share web site
Download and install a third-party application from the ServiceNow Store
