questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Installation > Methods: Selecting a 'Copy button' on the application record (B) is NOT a valid way to install an application — no such button exists. Valid installation methods include: installing from the Application Repository (A), downloading from ServiceNow Share (C), and downloading from the ServiceNow Store (D).

questions.stem: Using Custom UI test step in Automated Test Framework, which of the following is NOT a testable page component?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > ATF > Custom UI: Form field values (D) are NOT testable with the Custom UI ATF test step — they are 'testable by other test step categories' (the standard Forms test steps). The doc at p2190 explicitly lists form field values as untestable by Custom UI steps. Buttons (A), UI controls (B), and UI pages (C) are testable. (p2190)

questions.stem:
Why create Applications in ServiceNow?

a) To replace outdated, inadequate, custom business applications and processes b) To extend service delivery and management to all enterprise departments c) To allow users full access to all ServiceNow tables, records, and fields d) To extend the value of ServiceNow
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Development > Reasons: Valid reasons are a (replace outdated apps), b (extend service delivery), and d (extend ServiceNow value) — answer A. 'Allow users full access to all ServiceNow tables, records, and fields' (c) is false — applications provide controlled, scoped access, not unrestricted table access.

questions.stem: Flow Designer supports variable data types to store record data and complex data. Which of the following are supported variable data types? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Flow Designer > Variable Data Types: Three supported variable data types in Flow Designer are: Choice (A), Integer (C), and Array.Boolean (E). These are valid data types for Flow Designer variables. 'Freedom data type' (D) and 'Label data type' (F) do not exist. Array.Reference (B) may exist but is not the community-validated answer.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about Guided Application Creator?

options.text: The global scope option is turned on by default
Default access controls are automatically created
The welcome screen appears every time a new application is created
A scoped application user role is automatically created

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Guided Application Creator > Behavior: Default access controls are automatically created (B) when using the Guided Application Creator. The global scope option is not on by default (A is false). The welcome screen does not appear every time (C is false). Note: Community is at 50% — there is ambiguity between B and D (user role auto-created).

questions.stem: What are the ways to designate data tables when using Guided Application Creator (GAC)? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a new table on the platform
Use an existing table on the platform
Upload an existing word processing document

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Guided Application Creator > Table Options: Three ways to designate data tables in GAC are: create a new table on the platform (B), upload an existing spreadsheet (D), and use an existing table on the platform (E). PDF upload (A) is available in App Engine Studio with specific licensing, not standard GAC. Freeform database (C) and word documents (F) are not valid options. (p669)

questions.stem: What is the Event Registry?

options.text: A Workflow which is launched every time an Event is generated; used to debug Events
The Event Log which lists all Events that have been generated
The method used in server side scripts to generate Events and pass parameters
A table containing a record for every Event known to the ServiceNow system which allows ServiceNow to react when Events are generated

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Event Registry: The Event Registry is a table containing a record for every Event known to the ServiceNow system, which allows ServiceNow to react when those events are generated (D). It defines available event names and descriptions. It is NOT the event log (B - that's System Logs > Events), and not a workflow (A) or the eventQueue method (C).

questions.stem: Identify the ways an application can respond to an Event generated by the gs.eventQueue() method: (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Events > Responses: Two ways an application can respond to an event from gs.eventQueue() are Email Notification (B) and Script Action (D). Email Notifications can have an event-based trigger. Script Actions execute scripts in response to specific events. Client Scripts (A) are client-side and not event-driven. Scheduled Jobs (C) run on schedules. UI Policies (E) are form-based.

questions.stem: Is it possible to change an application’s scope?

options.text: Yes, but only from global scope to private scope
Yes, but only from private scope to global scope

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Scope: It is NOT possible to change an application's scope (A) after it has been created. Once an application is designated as private (scoped) or global, the scope is permanent. You would need to re-create the application in the desired scope. There is no mechanism in ServiceNow to convert between global and scoped.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about g_scratchpad? (Choose two.)

options.text: Used to push information from the server to the client
Does not exist on the mobile platform
Has default properties passed by client-side scripts

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > g_scratchpad: Two true statements about g_scratchpad: it is used to push information from the server to the client (A - populated in Display BRs, read by client scripts), and it has default properties accessible from client-side scripts (D). g_scratchpad does exist on mobile (B is false). It has no constructors or methods of its own (C is false).

questions.stem: Client-side scripts manage what?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Client-Side Scripts > Scope: Client-side scripts manage Forms and Form Fields (D). They execute in the user's browser to control field visibility, read-only status, mandatory requirements, and form interactions. Server-side scripts manage the database and backend (A/B). Access controls manage user access (A). Playbooks are workflow-related (C).

questions.stem: When debugging Email Notifications, what must you check on a user record? (Choose two.)

options.text: The Email field must have a valid value.
The user must not be locked out.
The First name and Last name fields must have values.

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Email Notification Debugging > User Record: When debugging email notifications, the two key user record checks are: Active must be true (A - inactive users receive no notifications) and the Email field must have a valid value (B - required for delivery). Locked out (C), name fields (D), and delegation (E) do not affect standard email notification delivery.

questions.stem: When crafting a scoped application that contains flow actions, what is the application called?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Flow Designer > Spoke: A scoped application containing flow actions dedicated to a specific application or integration is called a Spoke (B). Spokes package related Flow Designer content (actions, subflows, flows) for a particular integration. An Action (A) is a single step; a Bundle (C) groups catalog items; a Flow (D) is a complete automation process.

questions.stem: Which are reasons an application could be developed on the ServiceNow platform? (Choose three.)

options.text: It needs workflow to manage processes.
It uses forms extensively to interact with data.

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Development > Reasons: Three valid reasons to develop on ServiceNow are: it needs workflow to manage processes (A), it requires reporting capabilities (B), and it uses forms extensively to interact with data (C). Low-level programming libraries (D) are not a ServiceNow strength. Multimedia features (E) are not a primary ServiceNow use case.

questions.stem: Once an application is ready to share, which of the following methods of publishing are supported by ServiceNow? (Choose three.)

options.text: Publish to a local USB device

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Publishing > Methods: Three supported publishing methods are: Publish to an application repository (A), Publish to the ServiceNow Store (C), and Publish to an Update Set (D). The docs at p194 list Publish To App Repo, Publish To App Store, and Publish To Update Set as permissions available to delegated developers. Publishing to a local drive (B), spreadsheet (E), or USB device (F) are not supported.

questions.stem: What is required to link a ServiceNow application to a Git repository? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Source Control > Git Link Requirements: Three items required to link an app to a Git repository are: Password/credential (D), User name (E), and URL (F). The docs at p1147 confirm the fields needed: 'Git repository URL', 'Git username', and 'Personal access token' (password). URI (A) is not a separate field; ACL (B) is unrelated; Application name (C) is NOT required to link.

questions.stem: Which business requirements and process(es) should be documented as part of the application development plan? (Choose four.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > App Planning > Business Process Documentation: Four requirements to document are: Business problem (B), Process steps (C), Users/stakeholders (D), and Data input/output (G). These four define the core of a business process. Available licenses (A) and database capacity (E) are infrastructure/licensing concerns. Project schedule (F) is a project management artifact. (p615)

questions.stem: When creating application tables, a user role is automatically added to the table record. Which other role does an application typically have?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > App Roles > Typical Roles: When creating application tables, a user role is automatically added; the other typical role is Application Admin (C). ServiceNow applications conventionally include two roles: a user role for regular access and an admin role for managing the application. Application Super User (A), Fulfiller (B), and Manager (D) are not the standard role pattern created with app tables.

questions.stem: What data types of Flow Designer variables are supported to store record data and complex data? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Flow Designer > Variable Data Types: Three supported Flow Designer variable data types are Integer (B), Choice (D), and String (E). These are confirmed valid Flow Designer variable types. 'Label data type' (A) does not exist. Array.Reference (C) is not a standard supported type for this context. Integer, Choice, and String cover numeric, selection, and text data needs in flows.

questions.stem: What are the features of Flow Designer? (Choose three.)

options.text: Call a flow from another flow or subflow.
Test a flow using the “Run as” feature.
Support Java Scripting code to test conditions that trigger the flow.
Run a flow from a Catalog item.
Perform form field data validation at client side.

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Flow Designer > Supported Features: Three supported Flow Designer features are: Add stages to a flow (A), Test a flow using 'Run as' (C), and Run a flow from a Catalog item (E). Calling a flow from another flow (B) is NOT supported — you can call subflows but not other flows. Java Scripting to test conditions (D) is not a specific FD feature. Client-side form validation (F) is done via Client Scripts.

questions.stem: How is access to Application Menus and Modules controlled?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Menus > Access Control: Access to Application Menus and Modules is controlled with Roles (C). The docs at p2382 confirm: 'Roles Restricts access to the specified roles.' Access Controls (A) govern record/field security. Client Scripts (B) control client-side form behavior. Application Rules (D) is not a ServiceNow concept for menu access.

questions.stem: What is the ServiceNow App Repository?

options.text: A collection of files in a Git database

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > App Repository > Definition: The ServiceNow App Repository is a database containing ServiceNow apps (B). It is a central location where developed applications are published and from which they can be installed on other instances. It is not a Request table (A), a Git database (C — that is source control), or another name for update sets (D).

questions.stem: What happens to the List view when a new field is added to an existing table?

options.text: The new field is added at the start of the List
The new field is added at the end of the List
The new field is not added to the List view
A List View is created with the new Field

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > List Views > New Fields: When a new field is added to an existing table, the new field is NOT automatically added to the List view (C). List views must be manually configured to include new fields. The field is available in the table's dictionary but won't appear in existing list views until explicitly added. It's not added at the start (A), end (B), or in a new list view (D) automatically.

questions.stem:
Exportitem table is extended from Item Table with the additional column of ItemCountry added. The Item table contains the columns ItemName and ItemQty.

Which fields are available in the ExportItem Table?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Table Extension > Inherited Fields: The ExportItem table (which extends Item and adds ItemCountry) contains ItemName, ItemQty, and ItemCountry (B). Extended tables inherit ALL fields from the parent table plus any new fields added. Only ItemCountry (A) omits inherited fields. ItemCountry + Number (C) is incorrect. Only ItemName + ItemQty (D) omits the new field.

questions.stem: What data types of Flow Variables are supported to store record data? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Flow Designer > Variable Types for Record Data: Three Flow Designer variable data types for storing record data are: Array (C), Integer (D), and String (E). These are confirmed supported Flow Variable types. Choice (A) can be used for selections but is not specifically for record/complex data. Date (B) is not in the list of supported types for this purpose.

questions.stem: Which of the following objects does a Before Business Rule have access to in a script?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Business Rules > Before BR Objects: A Before Business Rule has access to current (A) as its primary scripting object — the GlideRecord representing the record being processed. While `previous` can be available for update operations, it is not universally available (not for insert), making `current` the reliable and standard object. GlideRecord is a constructor class, not a pre-defined BR variable.

questions.stem: Which options are strategies for debugging client-side scripts? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Client Scripts > Debugging: Two strategies for debugging client-side scripts are: g_form.addInfoMessage() (A) — displays visible messages on the form to show debug values — and jslog() (D) — logs to the browser's JavaScript console. gs.addErrorMessage() (B) and gs.log() (C) are server-side methods and are not available in client-side scripts.

questions.stem: In a privately-scoped application, which methods are used for logging messages in server-side scripts? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Scoped Apps > Logging: In a privately-scoped application, the logging methods for server-side scripts are gs.debug() (C) and gs.info() (D). gs.log() (B) is restricted in scoped apps (global-only). gs.logError() (A) is not a valid method. gs.error() (E) is valid in scoped apps but not the two the community confirms for this specific set. Scoped apps use gs.info/debug/warn/error.

questions.stem: When creating an application through the Guided Application Creator, what are the options for creating a table? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a table from a template

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > GAC > Table Creation Options: Three table creation options in the Guided Application Creator are: Create a table from scratch (D), Extend a table (F), and Upload a spreadsheet (G). The doc at p675 confirms spreadsheet upload. Import jobs (A), API calls (B), templates (C), and external table linking (E) are not GAC table creation options.

questions.stem: Which one of the following database operations can be controlled with Application Access? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Access > Controllable Operations: Two database operations controllable by Application Access are Update (B) and Create (C). The Application Access settings include Can read, Can create, Can update, and Can delete checkboxes. Query (A) cannot be controlled via Application Access — it is controlled through ACLs and before-query Business Rules. The question selects the two most commonly tested options.

questions.stem: Which is an example of when an application might use a Scheduled Script Execution (Scheduled Job)?

options.text: The application needs to run a client-side script at the same time every day.
The application needs to query the database every day to look for unassigned records.
To display a custom welcome message when a user logs in.
To validate form input fields before a record is submitted.

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Scheduled Jobs > Use Case: A Scheduled Script Execution is appropriate when an application needs to query the database daily for unassigned records (B). Scheduled Jobs run server-side on a defined schedule, making daily batch queries a perfect use case. They cannot run client-side scripts (A). Welcome messages on login (C) use Client Scripts. Form validation (D) uses Client Scripts or UI Policies.

questions.stem: What field type would you select if you want to query records from another table on a form?

options.text: Use the Phone Number field type.

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Field Types > Reference: Use the Reference field type (D) to query records from another table on a form. Reference fields link to another table and display a lookup picker, allowing users to search/select records from the referenced table. The doc at p1430 confirms: 'Reference fields ensure consistent data by normalizing data in another table.' Date (A), Phone Number (B), and String (C) do not reference other tables.

questions.stem: What functionality is supported by Flow Designer?

options.text: The role flow_operator can create and edit flows.
Flows can be "Run as” security admin.
Call a subflow from a flow.
Flows can trigger off a record being deleted.

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Flow Designer > Supported Functionality: Calling a subflow from a flow (C) is supported by Flow Designer. The docs confirm subflows can be invoked within flows using the Subflow step. flow_operator role can manage flows but not create/edit (A is false). 'Run as' runs as a specific user, not security admin (B is imprecise). Record-deleted trigger exists, but calling subflows from flows (C) is the documented supported feature. (p729)

questions.stem: Which method can be used to install an application on a ServiceNow instance? (Choose three.)

options.text: Install from the Google Play Store.
Download and install a third-party application from the ServiceNow Store.
Use the "Install" button on the application record.
Install an application from the Application Repository.
Import an application from an XML file.

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > App Installation > Methods: Three valid installation methods are: Download and install from the ServiceNow Store (C), Install from the Application Repository (E), and Import from an XML file (F). Google Play Store (A) and Stack Overflow (B) are not ServiceNow platforms. Using an 'Install' button on the application record (D) is not a standard installation method — the App Repo and Store have Install buttons, not generic app records.

questions.stem: Which one of the following is the correct Link Type to select when creating a module which opens the Record Producer UI for a user rather than the ServiceNow form UI?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Modules > Record Producer Link: The URL (from Arguments:) link type (A) is used to create a module that opens the Record Producer UI instead of a standard ServiceNow form. This allows specifying the Service Catalog record producer URL in the Arguments field. Content Page (B) and Script (C) don't support custom URL-based navigation to catalog items.

questions.stem: Which are valid caller access field options? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Caller Access > Valid Options: The three valid Caller Access field options are: Caller Tracking (A), None (C), and Caller Restriction (E). The doc at p85 lists these three as the available choices. 'Accessible from' (B) is a separate Application Access field; 'Allow Configuration' (D) is also a separate field; 'Caller Permission' (F) does not exist. (p85)

questions.stem: Which items are valid UI Action types in ServiceNow? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > UI Actions > Valid Types: Three valid UI Action types are: List banner button (A), Form button (B), and List choice (D). The doc at p2218 lists these among the valid types. 'Record navigation button' (C), 'Form choice' (E), and 'Workflow action' (F) are not valid UI Action types in ServiceNow. (p2218)

questions.stem: What occurs when an existing table is extended in ServiceNow?

options.text: The parent table's Access Controls are ignored when determining access to the new table's records and fields.
The new table does not inherit any of the fields from the parent table.
You must script and configure all required behaviors.
The new table inherits the functionality built into the parent table.

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Table Extension: When an existing table is extended, the new table inherits the functionality built into the parent table (D) — including fields, business rules, and access controls. Parent table ACLs are inherited (not ignored — A is false). New fields ARE inherited (B is false). Existing behaviors are inherited automatically (C is false). (p180)

questions.stem:
An application called My App has a table, MyAppTable, with this Application Access configuration:

Accessible from: All application scopes

Can read: Selected -

Can delete: Not selected -

Allow configuration: Selected -

Which of the following is true based on this configuration?

options.text: An application developer working in another privately scoped application can write a Business Rule for the MyAppTable table which successfully deletes all records from the MyAppTable table
An application developer working in the My App scope can write a Business Rule for the MyAppTable table which successfully deletes all records from the MyAppTable table
Any Application developer can write a Business Rule which successfully deletes all records from the MyAppTable
No Business Rule can be written which successfully deletes all records from the MyAppTable table

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Application Access > Delete Scenario: A developer in the My App scope can write a BR that successfully deletes records (B). Application Access restrictions apply to EXTERNAL scopes only — the owning scope is always unrestricted. An external scope developer CAN create a BR (Allow configuration=selected) but that BR cannot delete (Can delete=not selected). (p74)

questions.stem: How can Administrators expand the list of supported file types for code search in ServiceNow Studio?

options.text: By modifying the default code search table
By creating a new code search group
By adding new file types to a custom search group

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Studio > Code Search Expansion: Administrators can expand the list of supported file types for code search by creating a new code search group (C). Code search groups define which application file types are included in search. Modifying the default table (A), metadata sync settings (B), or adding to a custom search group (D) are not the correct approach.

questions.stem: What happens if a record producer script aborts the record generation process in ServiceNow?

options.text: Record creation displays an error message to the user
Record is not generated in the Item Produced Record table
Record creation is redirected to a confirmation page
Record creation terminates without notifying the user

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Record Producers > Script Abort: If a record producer script aborts the record generation process, record creation terminates without notifying the user (D). The process stops silently — no error message is displayed (A is false), no redirect to a confirmation page occurs (C is false). The record is not generated but the user receives no feedback about why.

questions.stem: What is a function of an update set in ServiceNow Studio?

options.text: To track and monitor system performance metrics
To manage configurations directly in a production environment
To group configuration changes for transfer between instances

questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Update Sets > Function: The function of an update set is to group configuration changes for transfer between instances (D). Update sets allow developers to bundle customizations in development and move them to test/production environments. They don't track performance metrics (A), create applications (B), or bypass change management to modify production (C). (p2609)

questions.stem: Which table in ServiceNow stores the details of customizations included in an update set?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Update Sets > Storage Table: The Customer Update [sys_update_xml] table (A) stores the details of customizations included in an update set. The doc at p2610 confirms: 'The customizations associated with the update set appear in the Customer Update [sys_update_xml] table.' The Update Set [sys_update_set] table (D) stores the update set record itself, not its contents. (p2610)

questions.stem: What is displayed to delegated developers to package changes for deployment in ServiceNow Studio?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Delegated Development > Deployment: Delegated developers see the Publish Button (C) in ServiceNow Studio to package their changes for deployment. The Publish Button allows developers to submit their application/changes to the repository or store. The Update Set Picker (D) is visible to non-delegated admins; the Tools tab (A) and Export to XML (B) are not the deployment packaging option.

questions.stem: How does ServiceNow match inbound email to existing records?
questions.explanation: [Platform] CAD > Inbound Email > Record Matching: ServiceNow uses two methods to match inbound email replies to existing records: Watermark (A) — a unique identifier embedded in the email thread, and Subject line with record number (C) — the record number (e.g., INC0001234) in the reply subject. Both mechanisms are used together for reliable email-to-record correlation.
